about.title: Oakley Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Oakley's collision numbers tell a familiar story: dozens of injury crashes each year along Main Street, Laurel Road, E Cypress Road, and Empire Avenue, with Saturday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. showing up often in public crash records. Behind each number is someone dealing with medical bills, missed work, and an insurance adjuster who wants a quick statement. LawProactive isn't a law firm — we're a free service that connects people injured in Contra Costa County crashes with independent attorneys who work these claims daily. They can help you understand what your medical records and repair estimates actually support, gather crash-scene evidence before it disappears, and deal with insurers so you don't have to navigate that alone. There's no cost to get connected, and any attorney you work with typically takes a fee only if you recover money. Reaching out early, before evidence fades or deadlines close in, tends to give you more options later.

whyChoose.title: Why Oakley Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: California's Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident lawsuit in California, but that window shrinks dramatically — sometimes to six months — if a government entity (like Contra Costa County) was involved. An attorney can flag this early so you don't lose your claim to a missed deadline.

items.title: Comparative Fault Means Your Story Matters
items.desc: California allows you to recover damages even if you were partly at fault, with your compensation reduced by your share of responsibility. An independent attorney can help make sure the insurer doesn't unfairly inflate your percentage of blame based on a hasty recorded statement.

items.title: No Cap on What You've Truly Lost
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases. That makes it worthwhile to have someone document the full impact of your injury rather than accept an early lowball offer.

items.question: Should I give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement?
items.answer: It's generally best to hold off until you've spoken with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to shift blame or minimize your injuries, and a recorded statement given early, before you know the full extent of your injuries, can hurt your claim later.

items.question: Why do so many crashes seem to happen on Saturday afternoons in Oakley?
items.answer: Public crash records show Oakley's reported collisions tend to cluster on Saturdays between roughly 3 and 5 p.m., a pattern consistent with heavier weekend traffic on corridors like Main Street and Empire Avenue. This is a neutral pattern in the data, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: What if my accident happened on a road maintained by the city or county?
items.answer: Claims involving government-maintained roads in Contra Costa County can carry a much shorter filing deadline than the standard two years, sometimes as little as six months. It's worth getting connected with an attorney quickly so this shorter window doesn't close before you've had a chance to file.
